For part 2, we need a.e. convergence. The plan: for each k ≥ 1, take ε = 1/k. There's a.e. x has eventually |fSeq(n+1)x - f x| < 1/k. Intersect over k. This gives a.e. convergence.

open scoped Topology MeasureTheory

theorem summable_measure_limsup_null_ae_tendsto
    {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] (μ : Measure α)
    (fSeq : ℕ → α → ℝ) (f : α → ℝ)
    (h :
      ∀ ε > 0, Summable (fun n : ℕ => μ {x | ε ≤ |fSeq (n + 1) x - f x|})) :
    (∀ ε > 0, μ {x | ∃ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ε ≤ |fSeq (n + 1) x - f x|} = 0) ∧
      ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => fSeq n x) Filter.atTop (nhds (f x)) := by
  have part1 : ∀ ε > 0, μ {x | ∃ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ε ≤ |fSeq (n + 1) x - f x|} = 0 := by
    intro ε hε
    have hsum := h ε hε
    exact MeasureTheory.measure_setOf_frequently_eq_zero hsum.tsum_lt_top.ne
  refine ⟨part1, ?_⟩
  -- For part 2: use countable intersection over ε = 1/(k+1)
  have hae : ∀ k : ℕ, ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, |fSeq (n + 1) x - f x| < (1 : ℝ)/(k+1) := by
    intro k

    exact hx

  have hn1 : n ≥ 1 := by omega
  have := hN (n - 1) hn'
  have hrw : n - 1 + 1 = n := by omega
